channel.title: The Local France - Article Feed
channel.description: Latest articles from The Local France (thelocal.fr)

item.title: Explained: Who owns all the second homes in France
item.description: Around 1 in 10 properties in France are used as a second home - but who owns them all? Here's the breakdown of age, wealth, nationality and region for France's holiday homes.

item.title: TELL US: Are you affected by tighter French citizenship rules for under 30s?
item.description: Recent changes to the rules on applying for French citizenship have made the process especially difficult for young people - even if they arrived in France as young children and spent their whole life here. We want to hear from young people (or their parents) affected by this.

item.title: French phrase of the day: Médaille en chocolat
item.description: This French phrase is less good than it sounds, and you don't even get any chocolate.

item.title: 8 articles to read before applying for a French 'visitor' visa
item.description: If you're a non-EU citizen moving to France, one of your first tasks is figuring out your visa. You may have heard that France's 'visitor' visa is among the easiest to get, but there are some important things to know before applying.

item.title: Explained: French VF and VOST films
item.description: If you browse film listings in France, you will notice that beneath each showing appears the initials VF or VOST - here's what that means.

item.title: Activists hang UK ex-prince's arrest photo in the Louvre
item.description: Activists managed to temporarily hang a new picture in Paris' Louvre - the arrest photo of UK royal family member Andrew Mountbatten-Windsor.

item.title: Everything you need to know about France's upcoming local elections
item.description: France heads to polls in March for local elections - from voting registration and proxy votes to the political effects on next year's presidential elections, here's what you need to know.

item.title: Everything that changes in France in March 2026
item.description: From municipal elections to a new parcel tax and an increase in vehicle registration, here is what is on the agenda for March 2026 in France.

item.title: France to revoke US envoy's govt access after summons no-show
item.description: France moved on Monday to block US envoy Charles Kushner from having access to government ministers, after he failed to show up to explain comments about a killed far-right activist.

item.title: French prosecutors ask for prison time over Ukraine graffiti
item.description: Prosecutors asked a Paris court Monday to sentence three Moldovan nationals to up to three years in prison for daubing coffins on public buildings in reference to the conflict in Ukraine.
